output.summary:
KEP-495 added an opt-in pod-level `ShareProcessNamespace` boolean so all containers in a pod share one PID namespace, with CRI updated to support Container, Pod and Node PID modes. The feature was hidden behind a feature gate, which was later removed in 1.19, and the KEP is recorded as implemented at stable stage.</summary>
<parameter name="rationale">The design addresses the lack of PID namespace sharing between containers in a pod, which had been an implicit API relied on by some images. The default of false keeps per-container PID namespaces, so existing `pid == 1` expectations stay backward compatible. A maintainer later reported the feature complete after the feature gate was removed in 1.19.

alternatives.option: Keep each container in a separate PID namespace with no pod-level option
alternatives.why_not: The motivation notes that an implicit API had formed around shared PIDs, so the design adds an explicit per-pod opt-in while keeping the default unchanged.

alternatives.option: Add a per-container PID sharing configuration
alternatives.why_not: Per-container configuration of PID namespace sharing is listed as a non-goal.

alternatives.option: Support multiple shared PID namespaces per pod
alternatives.why_not: Multiple shared PID namespaces per pod is listed as a non-goal.

evidence.quote: We will add support for configuring pod-shared process namespaces by adding a new boolean field `ShareProcessNamespace` to the pod spec.
The default to false means that each container will have a separate process namespace.
The only remaining item for this feature is to finish removing the feature gate in 1.19.
Looks like the PodShareProcessNamespace feature gate was removed in 1.19, anyway (#90096, @tedyu) This feature is complete.
The retroactive PR incorrectly called this "implemented" at beta, so it skipped PRR this cycle.
